## Project overview

TowerDefend is a public React and TypeScript project with a dedicated game-engine layer and a component-based interface. Its repository includes game entities, state and rendering modules, achievement and upgrade systems, audio and visual assets, an Express production entry point, and progressive-web-app configuration.

## Problem / goal

The project’s goal is to create an interactive browser game whose real-time mechanics, progression systems, interface state, and persistent player data remain coordinated as the application grows.

## What I built

The game engine manages waves, enemies, towers, bullets, collisions, targeting, rewards, and upgrade effects. Supporting modules handle achievements, player statistics, skill progression, audio, and browser storage, while React components provide the surrounding dashboard and controls.

The Vite PWA configuration adds an install prompt and offline app-shell caching. The repository documents local development, production builds, and static deployment preparation; it does not claim a live demo yet.

## Key features

- TypeScript game loop with separate engine, entity, state, HUD, and renderer modules
- Wave-based enemy spawning and tower targeting
- Upgrade, skill, achievement, and player-stat systems
- Persistent browser storage for player progress
- Responsive React interface and reusable UI components
- Audio, texture, geometry, and icon assets
- Installable PWA shell with offline caching
- Vite build process and Express production entry point

## Technologies

::: {.tag-list .tag-list-large}
<span>TypeScript</span><span>React</span><span>Vite</span><span>Tailwind CSS</span><span>Three.js / R3F</span><span>Express</span><span>PWA</span>
:::

## What I learned

TowerDefend demonstrates how real-time state differs from conventional page state. Game mechanics, rendering, progression, and interface feedback need clear boundaries while still responding to the same event loop and persistent player model.

## Future improvements

The repository marks the live demo as forthcoming. Additional next steps could include automated tests for progression rules, performance profiling across devices, and publishing the prepared production build.
